en: The Philippine eagle, the national bird, stands about one meter tall and has a wingspan of two meters.
The Philippines declared independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, after exactly 333 years of Spanish colonization.
The Philippine Congress is bicameral, consisting of 24 senators and up to 300 district and party-list representatives.
The Philippines has over 180 distinct languages, but Filipino and English are the two official national languages.
Jose Rizal wrote his famous final poem, "Mi Ultimo Adios," which contains exactly 14 stanzas of four lines each.
The Panagbenga Flower Festival in Baguio City lasts for exactly one month, featuring floats decorated with thousands of real flowers.
The Banaue Rice Terraces, built by the Ifugao people 2,000 years ago, sit at 1,500 meters above sea level.
Filipino scientist Dr. Ramon Barba invented a simple flowering technique for mangoes in 1974 using just potassium nitrate and water.
National Artist Napoleon Abueva, known as the Father of Modern Philippine Sculpture, created over 500 distinct artworks during his lifetime.
A Philippine president serves a single term of exactly six years, which is twice as long as a three-year local term.
The Philippines is an archipelago composed of exactly 7,641 islands, which is 441 more than the previously believed 7,200.
The 1987 Philippine Constitution, the current supreme law, contains exactly 18 articles detailing the structure and powers of government.
